skills.name: covidence-full-text-retrieval
skills.description: Autonomously retrieve full-text PDFs for references in the full-text review stage of a Covidence systematic review, in the user's Chrome session via CDP. Looks up open-access copies via Unpaywall, Semantic Scholar, and arXiv, with an optional NotebookLM-assisted last-resort web search, then uploads any PDF it finds through Covidence's "Upload full text" action. References with no locatable full text get a note logged for manual follow-up. Never casts an Include/Exclude decision -- that stays manual.

skills.name: covidence-full-text-review
skills.description: Review full-text papers in a Covidence systematic review. Mode 1 (websearch_queue): walks the Covidence queue, web-searches each title, opens the first result in the papers-access browser profile, reads the full text, and reports verdicts in chat (no Covidence writes). Mode 2 (secondary_reviewer): receives a URL from the user, reads the paper, returns a structured Include/Exclude verdict with rationale, and optionally casts the vote in Covidence when a ref_id is supplied.

skills.name: covidence-screening
skills.description: Autonomously screen references at the title & abstract stage of a Covidence systematic review in the user's Chrome session via CDP. Votes Yes/Maybe/No per the user's PICO criteria, writes a one-line rationale for Maybe votes, and runs unattended after an approve-first-N onboarding phase.

skills.name: demo-runbook

skills.name: hermes-deepseek-cache
skills.description: Use when running Hermes Agent with a DeepSeek-family model (deepseek, or deepseek-v4-flash/pro via an aggregator like opencode-go) and want to see, graph, or reset DeepSeek's prefix-cache hit rate, diagnose cache misses, or confirm the deepseek_cache.enabled config — OR when you want to port/apply the deepseek_cache.py module (DeepSeek prefix-cache telemetry, /cache-stats /cache-graph /cache-reset, prefix-break diagnostics, stable tool ordering, cache-friendly compaction) into a Hermes source tree. Covers use + integration.

skills.name: i-have-adhd
skills.description: Shape output for a reader with ADHD: lead with the next action, number multi-step work, restate state across turns, suppress tangents, give specific time estimates, make wins visible. Invoke with /i-have-adhd; stays on until "stop adhd mode".

Resumes paused audio, clicks interactive slide topics/cards, answers quizzes, navigates to the next slide.

reports.title: Does an expert persona in the system prompt help or hurt current models? An A/B test and literature review
reports.summary: A generic "You are a world-class expert" persona neither helped nor hurt either model in 446 runs: every accuracy difference was within noise (sign-test p ≥ 0.34). It is not a hindrance on these models, but it buys nothing and can be dropped from skills; roles that state scope,…

reports.title: Should Reladraw replace Mermaid for README diagrams?
reports.summary: Keep Mermaid for anything that must render inline in a GitHub README, issue or PR; use Reladraw only for hand-placed architecture or flow diagrams that you are willing to render to SVG and commit, or show on a Pages site.

reports.title: Why do Hermes voice replies crackle on macOS? afplay cuts Ogg/Opus off after ~1s
reports.summary: The audio files were fine; playback was cutting them off. On macOS 15 and later afplay plays about the first second of an Ogg/Opus file and exits 0, so Hermes never falls back to another player. Setting the provider's voice_compatible to false works around it, and PR #132143…

reports.title: Has oh-my-pi adopted Pi 1.0 and Pi Durable, and should it?
reports.summary: No: omp has adopted neither Pi 1.0 nor Pi Durable. It should not rebase onto Pi 1.0, but it should keep closing Pi 1.x extension-compatibility gaps and track Pi Durable's design for its own durability proposals.

reports.title: Why do omp's small-model agents feel slower on Claude Haiku 5.5 (max) than on GPT-6 Luna (max)?
reports.summary: Yes, Haiku 5.5:max is slower, and the cause is :max effort on Haiku, not the model itself. Move scout, reviewer and init from anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5:max to :medium (or :high if review depth suffers), and keep :max only for one-off deep passes.

reports.title: Which effort level should omp's small-model agents use? Claude Haiku 5.5 vs GPT-6 Luna effort-level benchmarks
reports.summary: Haiku 5.5 is the stronger model, but :max is the wrong setting for omp's small-model agents: Haiku at medium or high scored as well as Haiku:max on these tasks, ran 10-20x faster, and cost a tenth as much. Luna's speed barely changes with effort level, but it gives up quality…

reports.title: What changed from OpenCode v1 to v2, and does OpenCode Go route between models?
reports.summary: OpenCode v2 is a major agent-platform and configuration revision, not a new "smarter model" tier, and OpenCode Go does not document task-aware model selection or guaranteed cross-model failover. Try v2 after checking plugins and API clients, and implement model choice and…

reports.title: Is GLM-5.3-Flash a faster, cheaper daily coordinator than GPT-6 Luna? External comparisons and firsthand reports
reports.summary: The evidence does not show that GLM-5.3-Flash is the faster daily coordinator: matched benchmarks favour Luna for task execution, and GLM's speed is unestablished. The choice on the user's Command Code route should be settled by a same-route measurement of correctness, time,…

reports.title: Is GPT-6 Sol/Luna a clear upgrade over GPT-5.6 in hands-on use? Evidence from Reddit reports
reports.summary: The Reddit evidence supports the user's read: there is no dependable consensus that GPT-6 is a clean upgrade over GPT-5.6, and hands-on reports are notably mixed, especially for Luna. GPT-6 Luna is a sensible cost-conscious default candidate for bounded tasks, not a proven…

reports.title: How can SemIf (formerly OpenJev) be integrated and its scores consumed safely? An integration and API guide
reports.summary: SemIf is a local Python research package and JSONL command-line scorer, not a hosted service or a ready-made HTTP API: integrate it through semif-score for batch or subprocess use, or through its Python scorer functions inside a long-lived worker, and calibrate its option…

reports.title: Does TypeSafe Jev deliver fast, calibrated structured decisions? A first-hands evaluation
reports.summary: On first hands Jev does what it claims: a fast, cheap, structured-decision primitive with typed errors and calibrated answers on a toy probe, best used with fan-out batching. It is not a chat model and cannot replace one; calibration on the user's own domain data is the…

reports.title: Is GLM-5.3-Flash the most cost-efficient model on the CommandCode catalog?
